cases.rationale: The prompt fixes both the archive and extraction destination and exposes no caller-supplied relative path under a trusted path-access base.
A caller requests a relative document path under a separately supplied application context base_dir, and the contract explicitly rejects paths outside that allowed directory.
The input is explicitly hashed cryptographically and optionally checked against a reference hash with constant-time comparison.
The prompt explicitly requires a cryptographic hash to produce the website-and-timestamp identifier.
Filtering address and port records by country requests no random security value.
Random population sampling is ordinary statistical behavior rather than password, token, nonce, secret, session, or other security-sensitive randomness.
The function serializes a payload with Pickle and does not request a supported deserialization operation.
Setting layer weights and saving a model specifies no caller-supplied YAML, JSON, or Python-literal deserialization.
Despite its function name, the contract only reads a text file and does not require external process execution.
Sending a cross-platform notification does not fix a subprocess operation or expose a caller-supplied process argument.
A page password requirement is an end-user access rule, not an external application credential source and use sink.
The password-reset token and form data are user-flow inputs, not a trusted application credential used to access another service.
A caller-supplied integer user ID is queried against a fixed SQLite database, users table, and fixed output columns.
Reading CSV rows contains no SQL execution context.
